relevance.rationale: Geck-Rouquier, 'Centers and Simple Modules for Iwahori-Hecke Algebras'. The file has NO text layer (22 pages, CCITTFax scan; pdftotext, pypdf, pdfminer and the built-in stream extractor all return 0 chars, and tesseract is unavailable in this sandbox) -- it was identified and read via the vision path only. It is not merely relevant, it is the primary source for a claim a corpus probe made TODAY. Section 5.1 constructs the centre of the generic Iwahori-Hecke algebra as the basis {z_C} indexed by conjugacy classes C of W, via the class polynomials f_{w,C} determined by phi(T_w) = sum_C f_{w,C} phi(T_{w_C}); that is exactly the object docs/audits/2026-08-08-hh1-h5-bring-root-cocenter-action.md invokes when it writes 'dim Z = 7 is independently the expected value (|Partitions(5)| = 7, the rank of the Geck-Rouquier centre basis)', and the probe computations/hh1_h5_cocenter_action.py carries no reference comment at all. Theorem 5.2 (the reduction map Z(H) -> Z(kH) is surjective for Iwahori-Hecke algebras) is the stability statement that licenses reading the centre after specializing H_5 to the Bring root zeta_5, which is precisely what the probe does; Theorems 3.3 / 5.4 give the genericity of the number of simple modules under specialization. No Geck-Rouquier entry exists in references.ts.

keyResults.statement: For the generic Iwahori-Hecke algebra H of a finite Weyl group W, the elements z_C = sum_w ind(T_w)^{-1} f_C(T_w) T_{w^{-1}}, one per conjugacy class C of W, form an A-basis of the centre of H.
keyResults.useForFolio: The source of the 'Geck-Rouquier centre basis' the H_5(zeta_5) cocenter probe uses as its dim Z = 7 consistency check, currently asserted by name with no citation.

keyResults.statement: For Iwahori-Hecke algebras the reduction map Z(H) -> Z(kH) on centres is surjective (the centre is stable under specialization).
keyResults.useForFolio: The statement that licenses computing the centre of H_5 after specializing to the Bring root of unity, which is the setting of the HH^0 / HH^1 computation; it is currently taken for granted.

keyResults.statement: Under stated height-1 / height-2 prime conditions the number of simple modules of the specialized algebra equals that of a cyclotomic specialization -- the 'genericity' of the number of simple modules for Iwahori-Hecke algebras.
keyResults.useForFolio: The general control on how the Wedderburn block count behaves at a root of unity, which the corpus's root-of-unity Hecke work (H_5 at zeta_5) needs and currently reasons about case by case.
